I have been farming these 7 mu for 45 years, and at 64 years old my wife and I can't manage too much heavy labor anymore. Cotton pays the best cash but needs the most work, so I keep it to 3 mu. The other 4 mu I do wheat-maize double cropping — wheat in winter for our own flour, then maize right after harvest for feed and sale. I don't try fancy new methods; I do what has worked year after year. For cotton I rotary till in April and put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, topdress once at flowering, irrigate twice, and spray insecticide around 12 times because the bollworm never gives up. Wheat gets more fertilizer — about 180 jin of compound per mu split as basal and jointing topdress — plus four irrigations and two pesticide sprays. For maize there is no time to till after wheat comes off, so I no-till plant directly in mid-June, use about 100 jin of compound per mu, and irrigate twice. I expect roughly 550 kg of seed cotton, 1000 kg of wheat, and 1100 kg of maize per mu if the weather is normal.
